[33m#S3[0m Add an opt-in `respectQueryAndFragment` flag to `cleanDoubleSlashes` so `//` inside the query string and fragment is preserved, with the default behaviour unchanged and tests added. (Nov 4, 12:51 AM)


[34mInvestigated:[0m Searched `src`, `test`, and `README.md` for `cleanDoubleSlashes` and `respectQueryAndFragment`. Read the trailing-slash helpers (`hasTrailingSlash`, `withoutTrailingSlash`, `withTrailingSlash`) in `src/utils.ts`, which already accept the flag. Read the existing `cleanDoubleSlashes` implementation, its README entry, its JSDoc, and `test/double-slash.test.ts`. Checked `parsePath` in `src/parse.ts`.

[33mLearned:[0m `cleanDoubleSlashes` splits on `://`, collapses `/{2,}` in each segment, and rejoins, so it has no notion of query or fragment. The trailing-slash helpers use `#` and `?` splitting when the flag is set and plain string operations otherwise. The existing tests covered only path and scheme cases.

[32mCompleted:[0m `cleanDoubleSlashes(input, respectQueryAndFragment?)` in `src/utils.ts` now finds the first `?` or `#`, cleans only the prefix, and keeps the suffix when the flag is `true`. Without the flag, the original logic runs. The JSDoc gained a description and example. The README entry was renamed to the new signature with a new example. `test/double-slash.test.ts` gained a `respectQueryAndFragment` block with six table cases and a default-behaviour test. Prettier was run on the changed files. `test/double-slash.test.ts` passes 12 of 12 tests, and `tsc --noEmit` reported no errors. Nothing has been committed. The full test suite has not been run.

[35mNext Steps:[0m The session is ongoing. The next likely step is to run the full test suite to check for regressions beyond the double-slash tests. Any further requests from the user have not yet been seen.

[36mNotes:[0m The flag name matches the trailing-slash helpers, so the API is consistent across the utils. The default path is untouched, so existing callers are unaffected. Only the targeted test file has been run, so broader coverage is still unconfirmed.
